label: S. 5244

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The SUSTAIN 340B Act amends the Public Health Service Act and the Social Security Act to update, regulate, and increase transparency within the 340B drug discount program. The bill establishes new requirements for contract pharmacies, defines patients eligible for 340B drugs, sets rules for child sites, creates a data clearinghouse to prevent duplicate discounts, prohibits discrimination by health plans or pharmacy benefit managers against 340B entities, and introduces a user fee program to fund federal oversight.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new patient definitions, strict child site eligibility rules, annual reporting of savings and financial assistance policies, contract pharmacy oversight, and future user fee assessments.

Required to offer 340B ceiling prices and deliver drugs to contract pharmacies without imposing prohibited conditions, while gaining rights to request audits of covered entities under specific criteria.
Subject to formal registration, standard contract provisions, audits, annual recertification, and rules requiring cancellation if no drugs are dispensed in a 12-month period.
Prohibited from discriminating against 340B entities or pharmacies through lower reimbursements, specialized fees, or network exclusions, and required to interface with the new data clearinghouse.
affected_groups.group: Group Health Plans, Health Insurance Issuers, and PBMs

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for standardized transparent financial assistance policies and sliding fee scales at covered entities, child sites, and contract pharmacies.

key_provisions: Establishes contract pharmacy regulations requiring written agreements, annual recertification, registration, minimum dispensing activity rules, standard contract provisions, and audit protocols.

Defines a 340B 'patient' based on having received an outpatient health care service within the preceding two years, maintaining an auditable medical record, and receiving a prescription resulting from that service or a valid referral.

Sets rigorous integration and operational rules for hospital child sites to remain eligible for the program, including meeting provider-based rules and enforcing a three-year eligibility delay for newly acquired sites.
Requires covered entities to report annually on program savings, patient financial assistance policies, patient demographics, and contract pharmacy data for public publication on an HHS website.

Establishes a 340B Drug Discount Program Data Clearinghouse via an independent third-party entity to collect claims-level data and prevent duplicate discounts between 340B pricing and Medicaid/commercial rebates.

Prohibits group health plans, health insurance issuers, and pharmacy benefit managers from discriminating against 340B entities and pharmacies regarding reimbursement rates, fees, or network restrictions.
Creates a mandatory user fee program starting in fiscal year 2031, assessing $50,000,000 annually (adjusted by CPI thereafter) on participating covered entities to fund administration and oversight.
missing_information: Specific regulatory details on how the Secretary will calculate exact individual entity user fee allocations beyond the total annual cap formula.
Exact criteria for hardship exemptions to the referral volume thresholds and child site acquisition delays.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SUSTAIN 340B Act amends the Public Health Service Act and the Social Security Act to update, regulate, and increase transparency within the 340B drug discount program. The bill establishes new requirements for contract pharmacies, defines patients eligible for 340B drugs, sets rules for child sites, creates a data clearinghouse to prevent duplicate discounts, prohibits discrimination by health plans or pharmacy benefit managers against 340B entities, and introduces a user fee program to fund federal oversight.
summary_detail.significance: The SUSTAIN 340B Act represents a comprehensive legislative overhaul of the federal 340B drug discount program. It introduces sweeping transparency, auditing, and compliance structures that alter operational requirements for safety-net healthcare providers, drug manufacturers, retail pharmacies, and health insurance payers alike. The potential impact spans the entire financial and operational framework of the multi-billion-dollar drug discount program, affecting how covered entities manage discounts, contract pharmacies, patient qualifications, and program savings reporting.
